title: Who pays
hook: adult Muslims with wealth above the threshold for a full lunar year

segments.voice: Yesterday, zakat: a word that means to purify and to grow. Today, who pays it.

Mu'adh ibn Jabal is packing for Yemen. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is sending him to teach, and before he leaves, he gets his instructions, in order. The report is in Sahih al-Bukhari. First, call the people to the testimony. If they accept that, teach them the prayers. And if they accept that, tell them Allah has made a charity obligatory on them, taken from their rich and given back to their poor. From their rich, to their poor: in a handful of words, the answer to a question that sounds simple and isn't. Who actually pays zakat?
screen: `MU'ADH, PACKING FOR YEMEN.` → `TESTIMONY, THEN PRAYER, THEN ZAKAT.` → `FROM THEIR RICH, TO THEIR POOR.`

segments.voice: First, it's a duty for Muslims. The Qur'an sets it right beside the prayer. In surah two, in Pickthall's words: "Establish worship, pay the poor-due, and bow your heads with those who bow." Zakat is part of the practice of Islam, so it's asked of Muslims, not of their neighbors. Second, it's asked of the rich, in the Prophet's sense. Not a millionaire: someone whose wealth passes a set line, the threshold, which gets its own day tomorrow. Below that line, nothing is owed. A person who barely has enough is one of the people zakat is meant to reach, not one it's taken from. Third, the wealth has to sit. A hadith in the Sunan of Abu Dawud says no zakat is due on wealth until a year has passed over it. Money that comes in and goes straight back out to rent and groceries isn't what's counted. What stays is. It's a yearly reckoning, not a toll on every paycheck. Fourth, the hard edge: who counts as an adult owner? Here the schools of law differ, and say so plainly. On savings held by a child, the Hanafi school says no zakat is due. Other schools say it is due, and a guardian pays it from the child's wealth. Shia jurists have their own rulings again. Nobody here is ranked; each answer comes with its own reasons. Put together, the picture is narrower than people sometimes assume. Not everyone pays, and not on every dollar. A Muslim, past the line, on wealth that stayed a year, gives a share.
screen: `A DUTY OF MUSLIMS.` · `ON THOSE PAST THE LINE.` · `ON WEALTH THAT STAYED A YEAR.` · `WHO COUNTS AS THE OWNER?` · then, large: `ESTABLISH WORSHIP, PAY THE POOR-DUE.`

segments.voice: Without opening any app, ask yourself quietly: is there money that has stayed with me, untouched, for a long while, roughly how much, and is it more than I need to live on? If you're Muslim, those questions are the start of working out your zakat. If not, they're still a gentle way to see what you've been keeping, with no judgment.
Who pays. A Muslim whose wealth is past the threshold and has stayed a year. Taken from the rich, given to the poor. Today's word.
Your line: a share once a year. From the rich, to the poor, once the year has passed. Day one thousand ninety-four.

howItsDone: Muslims whose savings pass the threshold and have been held a year work out their zakat once a year, and those unsure of their school's rules, for example on a child's savings, ask a scholar or a zakat body.

chat.says: Does every Muslim have to pay zakat, even a student who's barely getting by?
options: Only if their wealth passes the threshold and stays a year; below the line, nothing's owed.
Yes: every adult Muslim pays a share of every paycheck, whatever they earn.
No: only people who own gold have to pay; cash and savings never count.
chat.meaning: Zakat is taken from the rich in the Prophet's sense: wealth past the threshold, held a year. Someone who barely has enough is who it reaches.

notes: Pickthall 2:43 quoted from memory; his text continues '(in worship)' after 'who bow'. Confirm wording.
Bukhari 1395 (Mu'adh sent to Yemen): confirm number; the same hadith also appears as Bukhari 1458 and 1496 in some numberings.
Abu Dawud 1573 (no zakat until a year passes): confirm number and grading.
Children's wealth: Hanafi no; Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali yes via guardian. Confirm, and confirm the Ja'fari position is fairly summarized only as 'their own rulings'.
